chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about purchasing the land of the People of the Covenant (Ahl al-Dhimma). He said, 'There is no harm with it, so it will be, as that is in their station, he pays as they pay.'

And a man from the people of the Nile asked him about a piece of land he had purchased at the mouth of the Nile from the people of the land, who said, 'It is their land,' and the people of al-Ustan (1) said, 'It is from our land.' He said, 'Do not buy it except with the consent of its people.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the Covenant (non-Muslims living under Islamic rule)
key_terms.أَهْلِ الْأَرْضِ: The people of the land (local inhabitants/owners)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on buying land from non-Muslims (Ahl al-Dhimma) and how are taxes handled?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that purchasing land from Ahl al-Dhimma is permissible provided the buyer assumes their existing tax liabilities (kharaj), ensuring continuity in fiscal obligations. It further introduces a crucial principle of *istihsan* (juridical preference) or caution in cases of conflicting ownership claims, requiring the buyer to secure the consent of all legitimate claimants to avoid future disputes. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on both legal validity and social harmony in property transactions within a pluralistic Islamic society.
